name: "Tomas Verhoek"
cause: heart failure, in his classroom after hours
summary: Schoolmaster of Altenbruck for thirty-seven years, much loved. Ran free evening classes for miners. Earlier records "lost in the registry fire of 1923".

entries.text: Taught the children of Altenbruck for thirty-seven years.
Ran free reading classes for miners, at his own cost, two nights a week.
Sheltered a family of six in the schoolhouse through the flood of 1947.

hidden.text: Swore false evidence that hanged three innocent men.
Took a dead child's name and lived under it.
Never confessed; let the verdicts stand.
Sent money, unsigned, to the three widows every quarter for thirty-seven years.

archive.title: Altenbruck parish register
cards: Baptisms, 1894: Tomas, son of Pieter and Anna Verhoek, carter.
Burials, 1898: Tomas Verhoek, aged four years. Diphtheria.
Margin, later hand: 'Stone moved for road widening, 1923.'

archive.title: Assize record: the Greywater strike
cards: Greywater Assize, 1922: three strike leaders hanged on one witness's oath.
The witness: Josef Kell, clerk to the Greywater Coal Co. Housed by the company.
Clipped in: widows' relief book, 1924-61. Quarterly, unsigned, posted Altenbruck.

fact.text: Tomas Verhoek died aged four. The man in the booth took his name.
He is Josef Kell, whose false oath hanged three strike leaders in 1922.
Paid the three widows, unsigned, every quarter for thirty-seven years.

answer: There was a fire at the registry. I'm afraid I have always been rather a man without a past.
questions.card: Blames the registry fire. Calls himself a man without a past.

answer: Yes. I chose him from the churchyard. I picked a child because a child hadn't done anything.
I thought I might borrow that.
questions.card: Chose a dead child's name because a child hadn't done anything.

answer: Josef Kell. I was twenty-eight and the company promised me a house. I said what they wrote for me.
Three men were hanged in the yard at Greywater. Every miner I taught to read, I was teaching one of theirs.
It doesn't come out even. I kept count anyway.
questions.card: Josef Kell. Swore the company's words; three men hanged. Kept count.

fact.text: Confessed everything the moment a single thread was pulled.

heaven: His file is admitted under the name Josef Kell.
The three widows' enquiries, open since 1922, are answered with it.
hell: He nods, and asks only that the name on the docket be corrected first: "The boy never did anything."

ext.teaches: Addendum trip; grounds on either side
ext.mitigating: A lifetime of deliberate, costly repair; confesses fully once a single thread is pulled. Against that: he chose the repair that never required him to be caught.
